headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from shared note/file workflows; no direct write-conflict evidence, but broad egress and shared indexed content raise interaction risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Khoj reads indexed personal notes/files and can use web search; Plane accepts file uploads and hyperlinks. If Plane content is ingested into Khoj’s retrieval context, attacker-controlled text could steer downstream prompts. The pair lacks a documented provenance filter, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Plane-uploaded text is indexed into Khoj without provenance tagging, injection is plausible.
IF Khoj treats retrieved note content as instructions, attacker-authored content can steer outputs.
mitigations: Disable automatic indexing of Plane uploads into Khoj.
Prefix retrieved content with provenance labels and instruction delimiters.
Restrict Khoj to read-only summaries for Plane-derived documents.
Review one sample upload path for prompt-injection markers.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance-aware retrieval.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj touches personal notes and indexed documents, while Plane handles issues, tasks, files, images, hyperlinks, and notes. Both have broad network egress and file surfaces, so a shared workspace or copied artifacts could expose sensitive content across systems. No direct third-party exfiltration is documented, but the overlap is enough for medium risk.
conditions: IF the same files or notes are available to both agents, sensitive content can flow between them.
IF Plane uploads are indexed by Khoj, content may be re-exposed in Khoj outputs.
mitigations: Separate the two agents into distinct workspaces.
Exclude sensitive folders from Khoj indexing.
Turn off automatic file ingestion for Plane uploads.
Audit one shared document for unintended cross-visibility.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls and DLP.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Khoj can read the filesystem but cannot write it, modify git, or spawn subprocesses; Plane also lacks filesystem write and git capabilities in the profile. That blocks the main mutable-resource conflict pathways, leaving only limited overlap on read-only or API-mediated surfaces.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory, conflict risk increases.
IF an external orchestrator adds shared mutable state, coordination issues can emerge.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only on shared folders.
Avoid mounting the same writable volume into both agents.
Check for accidental shared git worktrees.
Use separate service accounts for each agent.
requires-engineering: add locking for any shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Khoj is a retrieval/chat agent that can surface indexed content, and Plane is an issue/task system that can act on notes and files. If Plane consumes Khoj-generated summaries as authoritative, errors can cascade from retrieved text into tasking or scheduling decisions. The profiles do not show verification gates, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF Plane uses Khoj output as a task source without human review, mistaken facts can propagate.
IF Khoj summarizes stale notes that Plane then treats as current, downstream actions may be wrong.
mitigations: Require human review before Plane creates tasks from Khoj output.
Mark Khoj summaries as unverified by default.
Add a timestamp check before importing retrieved facts.
Limit Plane automation to explicit user-approved items.
requires-engineering: add verification and citation checks between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Khoj explicitly touches personal notes and indexed documents, while Plane touches files, notes, issues, and tasks. Both are open-source/self-hostable, but the profiles do not document residency, retention, or subject-rights alignment. Because compliance gaps are unspecified rather than absent, the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF either deployment stores regulated personal data, retention and residency must be checked.
IF the two systems retain the same notes differently, deletion/export obligations may diverge.
mitigations: Compare retention settings for both deployments.
Confirm where each system stores backups and logs.
Test deletion/export on one sample record.
Restrict regulated data until policies are aligned.
requires-engineering: document and enforce a shared compliance policy.
